episodes.title: SA demands action from federal government on aged care

stories.story: South Australia demands federal action on aged care bed blockages
stories.angle: Aged care crisis in South Australia putting immense pressure on the broader health system and requiring immediate federal intervention.
stories.voices: Presenter (live), Blair Boyer, SA Minister for Health (live)
stories.tone: Urgent and explanatory. The presenter questioned the minister on systemic failures, while the minister framed the issue as a long-term demographic challenge requiring federal funding.
stories.emphasis: Systemic strain, hospital bed blockages, and the human cost of elderly people waiting in emergency departments for residential aged care beds.
stories.placement: Lead item, covering the top of the program.
stories.evidence: We have known what the aging profile of Australia is going to be for a long, long time.

episodes.title: Does the new UK-EU deal signal the end of Brexit?

stories.story: UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak hails new UK-EU deal
stories.angle: Whether the new reset deal signals a significant shift in post-Brexit UK-EU relations or is merely a modest adjustment with limited economic impact.
stories.voices: Presenter (live), Rob Watson, BBC World Service political correspondent (live)
stories.tone: Analytical and skeptical. The presenter pressed on the practical limitations of the agreement, while the correspondent highlighted the political and trade hurdles.
stories.emphasis: Trade impacts, political motivations, and the reality of post-Brexit economic friction.
stories.evidence: It's pretty modest in and every other way, and it's not going to change the world.

stories.story: Debate over UK-EU deal and future economic impacts
stories.angle: Assessing the political fallout and whether the deal marks a turning point or a permanent stagnation in UK-EU relations.
stories.voices: Presenter (live), Rob Watson, BBC World Service political correspondent (live)
stories.tone: Conversational and speculative, examining the political rhetoric versus economic reality.
stories.emphasis: Political legacy, sovereignty concerns, and the difficulty of reversing Brexit-related friction.
stories.placement: Second segment continuing the Brexit discussion.
stories.evidence: The Brexit debate is back in a more general sense rather than just to do with this particular deal.

episodes.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as chief executive of Nvidia

stories.story: Jensen Huang reinstated as chief executive of Nvidia
stories.angle: The stunning reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO following revelations of extra-marital affairs, highlighting the growing influence of AI and tech giants on global markets.
stories.voices: Presenter (live), Isaac, technology reporter, Silicon Valley (live)
stories.tone: Fascinated and bewildered. The presenter questioned the board's decision-making, while the reporter analyzed the broader implications for the tech industry.
stories.emphasis: Corporate governance, executive power, and the dominance of artificial intelligence.
stories.placement: Second main segment of the program.
stories.evidence: It's a real fascinating move and basically stunned certainly stunned all of the business reporters out in Silicon Valley.

episodes.title: Treasurer flags 'substantial savings' in mid year budget update

stories.story: Treasurer Jim Chalmers flags substantial savings in mid-year budget update
stories.angle: Treasurer Jim Chalmers forecasting softer economic growth, higher inflation, and higher unemployment while committing to savings and addressing structural budget challenges.
stories.tone: Direct and adversarial. The presenter challenged the Treasurer on the adequacy of savings and the economic outlook, while the Treasurer defended the government's fiscal strategy.
stories.emphasis: Economic forecasts, cost-of-living pressures, inflation, and government spending restraint.
stories.evidence: We've got to deal with some of the structural pressures on the budget.

episodes.title: Pacific was heard in COP-31 climate talks, Prime Minister Albanese says

stories.story: Pacific nations make their voices heard at COP-31 climate talks
stories.angle: Assessment of the COP-31 climate talks outcome, focusing on the friction between Pacific nations demanding accelerated fossil fuel phase-outs and major economies pushing back.
stories.voices: Presenter (live), Anthony Albanese, Prime Minister (clip), Dr George Carter, Director of theANU Pacific Institute (live)
stories.tone: Serious and diplomatic. The presenter explored the geopolitical tensions, while the guest expert analyzed the Pacific's bargaining power.
stories.emphasis: Climate diplomacy, fossil fuel phase-out commitments, and the strategic positioning of Pacific island states.
stories.evidence: Climate change is the first, second and third priority of Pacific leaders.

episodes.title: ‘Fake Blak’: The Greens’ bitter civil war over Aboriginal identity

stories.story: The Greens' bitter internal conflict over Aboriginal identity and 'Fake Blak' allegations
stories.angle: An in-depth investigative look into the internal turmoil within the Australian Greens party over allegations of cultural appropriation and Indigenous identity fraud.
stories.tone: Investigative and somber. The presenter navigated a sensitive cultural issue with serious journalistic rigor.
stories.emphasis: Party politics, Indigenous representation, authenticity standards, and internal party conflict.
stories.evidence: Growing numbers of Greens members are identifying as Aboriginal, and they're getting a discount on their membership fees for ticking the box.

episodes.title: Has climate action stalled?

stories.story: Analysis of COP-31 climate summit outcomes and international friction over fossil fuels
stories.angle: Evaluating whether global climate action has stalled following COP-31, examining the fierce debate between developed nations and oil producers over fossil fuel phase-out language.
stories.voices: Presenter (live), Sam Koslosky, co-host (live), Emma Gillespie, co-host (live), Nicolette Bulla, Federal MP (clip)
stories.tone: Analytical, accessible, and conversational. The hosts broke down complex international climate negotiations into relatable insights.
stories.emphasis: International climate targets, diplomatic gridlock, fossil fuel lobbying, and the domestic political challenges of emissions reduction.
stories.placement: Lead segment focusing on global environmental politics.
stories.evidence: Almost 200 countries ran two days into overtime and still couldn't agree on whether those words belonged on the page.
